A garden keeps its own time, and the paths that cross it follow the slope of the hill more than any plan drawn at a desk. Rain moves the gravel, roots lift the stones, and each spring the beds sit a little lower than they did before. The gate at the far end opens onto a lane that runs past two farms and an old mill, and after that the road climbs through birch and pine until the valley is out of sight. A garden keeps its own time, and the paths that cross it follow the slope of the hill more than any plan drawn at a desk. Rain moves the gravel, roots lift the stones, and each spring the beds sit a little lower than they did before. Nobody who walks there in the morning hurries, and the light comes in low across the wet grass.
